**Which vocabulary the sync speaks is the deployment's call.** Before writing
anything, the CLI reads
`GET /capabilities` once. A deployment that advertises\n`vocabulary.version: 2` gets every request with `x-mcpjam-eval-vocabulary:
2`\nand case bodies spelled canonically — `iterations` (the exact count),\n`legacyIterations` (the legacy floor, the same number)
and `assertions` —\ninstead of `repetitions` / `iterations` / `checks`. A deployment without the\ncapability block, or without th
e capabilities route at all, is spoken to in\nvocabulary 1, byte-for-byte as before. Nothing in the file changes either way:\nthe
dialect of the file and the vocabulary of the wire are independent.\n\nCases are synced in batches of at most 100 (`create_eval_ca
ses`). Every\ndeclared case is created or updated, including `disabled: true` rows. A case\nthe file **no longer declares** is del
eted from the hosted suite before\nlaunch. A case the file still declares but marks `disabled: true` is **kept,\nwith its history*
* — it is simply left out of the launch, so parking a flaky\ntest does not destroy its past results and re-enabling it later resum

es the
same case.
The run is scoped to the enabled cases either way. A file with no enabled
cases is refused (`NO_ENABLED_CASES
`) rather than launching the whole\npersisted suite. `--case` may only name an enabled case. A later run updates\nexisting cases b
y declared id and creates new ones. An enabled case that\noverrides `passThreshold` is refused: hosted grading is suite-wide. A\nd
isabled case with the same override is ignored, matching how repetitions\nare checked. Authored\n`defaults.toolPolicy` and non-emp
ty `defaults.validity` gates are refused at\nhosted CLI launch (`TOOL_POLICY_UNSUPPORTED` / the corresponding validity\nrefusal).
Hosted platform-authored suites do not currently have a backend\ntool-policy field or enforcement path, so the CLI does not upload
a suite that\nwould claim those guarantees. When supported by an eval runner, `toolPolicy`\nis enforced at execution time with de
nied tools kept visible but blocked;\nserver annotations are advisory and **UNTRUSTED**. The file's default count\n(`defaults.repe
titions`, or `defaults.iterations` in `schemaVersion: \"2\"`) is\ninherited per case and is not uploaded as a suite `minIterations
` floor.\nAuthored `defaults.systemPrompt` and `defaults.temperature` are uploaded as\nexecution defaults; omitted fields stay omi
tted so the platform applies its\nown defaults. `target.hosts` and `target.environment` are attached before\nlaunch. A file enviro
nment takes precedence over file hosts for that launch,\nwhile an explicit CLI target takes precedence over both. When an explicit
CLI\ntarget is provided (for example `--host`), the file's `target.hosts` are\n**not** synchronized to the suite's persisted host
attachments — the suite\nkeeps whatever hosts it already has. Host attachment synchronization only\nruns when no explicit CLI tar

get overrides the file. Environment attachment
synchronization is unaffected and always runs.

Without `--idempotency-key`, the
CLI mints a fresh UUID for every invocation\nand prints it to stderr before launch (`Eval idempotency key: <key>`). Each\ninvocat
ion therefore starts and bills a new run. To retry a launch whose\nresponse was lost — without starting a second run — pass the ke
y that was\nprinted: `--idempotency-key <printed-key>`. A replay is marked `deduped` in\nthe receipt and human output. `--notes` i

s not part of the key.

##### Imported cases: live tool resolution, and per-run approval

Every file run performs the same liv
e check `eval validate --project` performs,\n**before it writes anything**. It is not opt-in and there is no flag to skip\nit. A f

ile with no deterministic `toolCall` steps asks no question and pays no
round trip.

What happens when a deterministic referenc

e does not resolve depends on the
case:

| Case | Outcome |
| - | - |
| Selected (enabled, and named by `--case` if you used
it) | The launch **refuses before the suite is synced** — nothing is written and nothing is billed |\n| Imported, not selected | I
ts claim is rewritten to `unresolved` (keeping `sourceCaseKey`) and it is **still persisted**, so the hosted record says what MCPJ
am found rather than still asserting a claim about a missing tool |\n| Native, not selected | Left exactly as authored. A hand-wri
tten case never acquires an `import` block from this — \"somebody wrote this\" and \"something converted this\" are different fact

s |

Each target is checked on **its own** server set. `--host` is checked against
that host's configured servers rather than t
he file's, because that is the set\nthe run connects — validating `target.servers` would approve a tool the host\ncannot reach. A
host the FILE declares uses its own `servers` list when it\ndeclares one (those are attached to the host before launch) and the ho
st's\nconfigured set when the field is omitted. An explicitly empty `servers: []`\nis a real, empty set — it clears the attachment
before launch — and is\nvalidated as such, never as an omitted field. A step that pins `serverId` is resolved by id;\n`serverName

` is a display fallback and never overrides it.

If the run's target set cannot be enumerated before the suite exists
(`--all-t
argets`, `--compose-*`), or a host does not report a server set, or a\nhost pins a server the project no longer has, the launch re

fuses rather than
assuming the references are fine.

`--case` accepts a hosted row id, which does not exist yet when this check
\nruns. A selector this stage cannot map is therefore treated as possibly naming\nany enabled case, so an unresolved reference sti

ll refuses; the launcher
resolves the selector itself a moment later.

A selected `approximated` case refuses unless this invoc

ation approves it:

| Flag | Required | Description |
| - | - | - |
| `--allow-approximated <case...>` | No | Approve an `appr
oximated` imported case for **this run only**, by AUTHORED case id (`cases[].id`). Repeatable. `--file` runs only |\n| `--approval
-reason <text>` | With the above | Why the approximations are acceptable for this run. 1–500 characters after trimming; one reason

Checked before anything is billed, each with its own message: approving a
**native** case (nothing to approve), a
**claimed-exact** one (needs no\napproval), an **unsupported** or **unresolved** one (approval covers a case\nwhose behaviour was
approximated, not one whose behaviour is missing), a\n**disabled** or **unselected** one (the run will not execute it), an unknow
n\n| `--project <id-or-name>` | Project name or ID (defaults to the most recently updated project) |\n| `--all-projects` | List ac
ross every accessible project. Conflicts with `--project`. |\n| `--status <status>` | Filter by session status |\n| `--limit <n>`

### `cloud sessions send`

Send one message to a project's MCP servers and print the r
eply plus the raw tool calls, per-call latency and token usage — the telemetry a participant in the conversation cannot see.\n\n**
This spends model credits on every call.**\n\n`--idempotency-key` is required and must be **stable for the intent**, not regenerat
ed per attempt. It is what makes a retry safe: with the same key, a turn that already completed is replayed rather than re-run and
re-billed. A fresh key per attempt deduplicates nothing.\n\nOmit `--session` to start a conversation; pass the `sessionId` the co
mmand returns to continue one. A session created by `cloud sessions browser open` is initially unconfigured and accepts its model
configuration with its first send. After the first model turn, the session is configured: `--model`, `--environment`, `--server`,
`--no-servers`, `--system-prompt` and `--tool-mode` are then refused alongside `--session` rather than silently repinning it.\n\n|

Flag | Description |
| - | - |
| `--message <text>` | The message to send, as the user (required) |
